sentences.text: Ld. counsel for revisionists had argued that all the allegations made by the complainant with respect to demand of dowry are prior to the marriage and there is no evidence of any alleged torture of the complainant by the accused persons.
Ld. counsel had further argued that there are no specific dates on which the alleged demands were made.
He had argued that the allegations are omnibus and general in nature which cannot be said to fall under the definition of Section 498A IPC and therefore, the impugned order on charge be set aside.

4. On the other hand, ld. Addl. PP for the State/respondent had argued that specific allegations have been made by the complainant against all the three accused persons which have been considered by the learned Trial Court and therefore, the revision petition be dismissed.

sentences.text: I have heard ld. counsels for parties and carefully perused the record.
6. The complainant had given a hand written complaint against the accused persons.
The complainant got married to the accused Keyur Bhatnagar on 11.07.2008.
There are several allegations with respect to demand of dowry against father-in-law and mother-in-law prior to the marriage which are specific in nature.

Even after the marriage, the complainant has levelled following allegations against the accused persons:
(i) One incident of Haryali Teej and Karwachauth wherein the father-in-law had pressurized the complainant to call her parents to send money for the festivals in his bank account and due to non-fulfillment of same, she was scolded and abused and even her mother-in-law slapped her many a times.

There are further allegations of pulling her hair by mother-in-law in the same incident and also against husband with respect to scolding her by him when she refused to call her brother to ask for money.
(ii) It has been specifically stated that she was tortured in different manners for not bringing sufficient dowry.
She was sent to her parental home in India when she was pregnant and was abandoned by the family at that time which further shows cruelty.
(iii) There is further an incident of December, 2009 wherein the husband had demanded Rs.25 lakhs and slapped the complainant and asked her to remain in the parental house itself.

7. In the case Union of India vs. Prafulla Kumar Samal & Anr. 1979 AIR 366, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has Keyur Bhatnagar & Ors. vs. State & Anr.
observed as under:-
"Section 227 of the Code runs thus:-

sentences.text: 'If, upon consideration of the record of the case and the documents submitted therewith, and after hearing the submissions of the accused and the prosecution in this behalf, the Judge considers that there is not sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused, he shall discharge the accused and record his reasons for so doing.'

The words 'not sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused' clearly show that the Judge is not a mere post office to frame the charge at the behest of the prosecution, but has to exercise his judicial mind to the facts of the case in order to determine whether a case for trial has been made out by the prosecution.

In assessing this fact, it is not A necessary for the court to enter into the pros and cons of the matter or into a weighing and balancing of evidence and probabilities which is really his function after the trial starts.
At the stage of section 227, the Judge has merely to sift the evidence in order to find out whether or not there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.

The sufficiency of ground would take within its fold the nature of the evidence recorded by the police or the documents produced before the court which ex facie disclose that there are suspicious circumstances against the accused so as to frame a charge against him."
8.

In the case in hand, at this stage, the statement of complainant is sufficient to frame charge under Section 498A/34 IPC against all the three accused persons namely Keyur Bhatnagar (husband), Raj Bala Bhatnagar (mother-in-law) and Gyanesh Chander Bhatnagar (father-in-law).

Keyur Bhatnagar & Ors. vs. State & Anr.
9.

8. The revision petition is accordingly dismissed.
9. A copy of this order be sent to the concerned ld. Trial Court for information.
10. Revision file be consigned to Record Room after necessary compliance.
